Export a tibble as a publication-quality LaTeX table

Source: R/write_manuscript.R
export_latex_table.Rd

Produces a booktabs-style table using \\botrule instead of \\bottomrule. Cells, column names, captions and notes are treated as literal text and escaped once. Notes use a threeparttable environment. The document needs booktabs and, for notes, threeparttable; outside a publisher class defining \\botrule, add \\providecommand{\\botrule}{\\bottomrule} to the preamble.

Usage

export_latex_table(
  data,
  filename,
  caption,
  label,
  note = NULL,
  digits = 3,
  col_format = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A tibble/data.frame.

filename

Character. Output .tex path.

caption

Character. Table caption.

label

Character. LaTeX label (without the tab: prefix; it will be added). Use letters, digits, colons, periods, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

note

Character. Optional footnote text.

digits

Integer. Digits for numeric columns. Default 3.

col_format

Character vector. Column alignment spec (e.g. c("l", "r", "r")). Default NULL picks "l" for the first column and "r" for the rest.

Value

The LaTeX source, invisibly.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("xtable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  out <- tempfile(fileext = ".tex")
  export_latex_table(head(iris), out,
                     caption = "First rows of iris.",
                     label   = "iris")
  cat(readLines(out), sep = "\n")
  unlink(out)
}
#> ✔ LaTeX table: /tmp/RtmpqAQwFg/file186e7b5f777f.tex
#> \begin{table}[ht]
#> \centering
#> \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
#>   \toprule
#> Sepal.Length & Sepal.Width & Petal.Length & Petal.Width & Species \\ 
#>   \midrule
#> 5.100 & 3.500 & 1.400 & 0.200 & setosa \\ 
#>   4.900 & 3.000 & 1.400 & 0.200 & setosa \\ 
#>   4.700 & 3.200 & 1.300 & 0.200 & setosa \\ 
#>   4.600 & 3.100 & 1.500 & 0.200 & setosa \\ 
#>   5.000 & 3.600 & 1.400 & 0.200 & setosa \\ 
#>   5.400 & 3.900 & 1.700 & 0.400 & setosa \\ 
#>    \botrule
#> \end{tabular}
#> \caption{First rows of iris.}
#> \label{tab:iris}
#> \end{table}
#>
